rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Wide prompts split by logical move — paragraph breaks = cheapest scan-affordance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt-1 is correctly move-split into five paragraphs (context-setting / 'Read both...' / the four-dimension bulleted list / 'quote a specific moment, don't generalise' / the closing rank-ask). Prompt-2's third paragraph (curriculum/prompts/spot-gaps-build-the-loop-2.md, registry line 22 -- reached from this file's line-39 marker) fuses the report instruction with the rule's own explicitly-named null-case-fallback pattern in one un-split paragraph: 'Show me the line you cut and, in two sentences, why the diagnosis killed it. If every rule still holds under diagnosis, say so and stop.' The rule names 'If nothing earned itself, stop.' verbatim as a move-boundary that earns its own paragraph.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: In curriculum/prompts/spot-gaps-build-the-loop-2.md, break the paragraph before the null-case sentence: '...why the diagnosis killed it.' [blank line] 'If every rule still holds under diagnosis, say so and stop.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt-1's lead-in ('read both sessions and walk the diff between them') mirrors both the fence's literal opening imperative ('Read both.') and its own later 'Walk the diff across four dimensions' phrase verbatim -- a clean rhyme. Prompt-2's lead-in ('cut the one rule the diagnosis killed') mirrors the fence's SECOND sentence ('Find the one rule the two-session diagnosis showed is wrong... Cut it...') rather than its literal first clause ('Read ./CLAUDE.local.md and this session's scrollback...'). Read as a strict first-clause mirror this is a miss, but the fence's first clause is pure context-loading and the lead-in correctly foregrounds the load-bearing move (the cut) that is this exercise's actual teaching point -- rewriting the lead-in to open on 'read' would bury that point for a fence three sentences long. Treating this as a live rule-question rather than a finding: the obvious literal fix would degrade the artefact, so it is not filed as a REVISE.
